text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bombs were discovered on Wednesday at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport and at Subic Bay Freeport, where 18 Pacific rim leaders will gather for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit. (MANILA TIMES)

- Police on Tuesday arrested a Dutch and six Japanese nationals who allegedly breached security at the tightly guarded Clark international airport. Leaders of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum are due to meet in nearby Subic on Monday. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Senior officials of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum on Wednesday put the finishing touches to their ambitious plans to tear down trade and investment barriers in the region. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- A top intelligence official said on Wednesday he sees "no major security threat" to the 18 heads of state and government and the delegates attending the APEC meetings. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- Workers of the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co and ground crew of Philippine Airlines on Wednesday threatened to go ahead with a strike due to alleged refusal of their respective managements to grant their demands. The government has been pleading with labour unions not to go on strike while the APEC forum is on. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- Labour Secretary Leonardo Quisumbing said on Wednesday there would be no strikes during the five-day APEC meeting. Quisumbing said all pending labour disputes in commercial, utility and service firms, including Philippine Airlines, were nearing settlement. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Guerrillas from the Moro Islamic Liberation Front abducted early on Wednesday morning two nephews of Mayor Joel Maturan of Tipo-tipo town in the southern Philippines. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- Activists of various political shades on Wednesday raised clenched fists, shaved their heads and fasted as they opened their own fora to denounce free trade espoused by APEC. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
